explain.what: Whether the share price is above or below its average price over the last ~10 months.
explain.why: Big funds buy and sell around this line, so being above it usually means buyers are in control. It is slow: it confirms a turn after it has happened.
explain.score: The price is well below its long-run average: the long-term trend has turned down.

explain.what: Whether the shorter trend (last ~10 weeks) is running above or below the longer trend (last ~10 months).
explain.why: It shows whether the trend itself is turning, not just where the price is today.
explain.score: The shorter trend has dropped below the longer one: momentum has turned down.

indicators.name: GLD vs the S&P 500 (SPY), 3 months
indicators.measured: SPY over the same 63 trading days

explain.what: Whether gold has beaten or lagged the S&P 500 (SPY) over the last 3 months.
explain.why: Stocks are the main alternative use of the money; this shows which the market is favouring.
explain.score: Gold and the S&P 500 (SPY) have moved roughly in line.

indicators.name: Buying vs selling volume
indicators.measured: volume on up days ÷ down days, last 20 trading days

explain.what: Whether more shares change hands on days the price rises than on days it falls (last 20 trading days).
explain.why: Large investors leave footprints in trading volume; heavy buying days suggest they are accumulating.
explain.score: Trading is balanced between up and down days.

indicators.name: GLD gold held (tonnes), 20-day change
indicators.note: 1,056.5 tonnes on 1 Oct 2026 vs 1,056.6 tonnes on 2 Sep 2026.

explain.what: Whether investors are adding gold to GLD or taking it out over the last 20 trading days (tonnes held by the trust).
explain.why: Money moving into or out of the biggest gold fund is a direct read of investor demand, separate from the price.

indicators.name: Hedge funds' net long in gold futures, % of open interest (contrarian)
indicators.bull: in the bottom 20% of its 3-year range (washed out)
indicators.note: Read the other way round: crowded = bearish. Hedge funds hold a net 30.9% of all gold futures (report of 22 Sep 2026); 3-year range -6.1% to 40.6%.

explain.what: How heavily hedge funds are betting on gold futures, compared with their own range over the last 3 years (weekly CFTC report).
explain.why: Read the other way round: when nearly everyone is already long there are few buyers left and forced selling can hit hard (29 Dec 2025 week, GLD −4.4%); when they are out, the reverse.
explain.score: Hedge-fund positioning is middling: not crowded either way.

indicators.name: Dollar backdrop (shared macro)
indicators.measured: the dollar index 20 trading days earlier

explain.what: Whether the US dollar has strengthened or weakened over the last month.
explain.why: Gold is priced in dollars: a stronger dollar makes it dearer for everyone else, and drove 4 of gold's 10 worst weeks in 5 years.
explain.score: The dollar has strengthened: a headwind for gold.

indicators.name: Fed rate expectations (shared macro)
indicators.measured: net odds (cut minus rise) for the next Fed meeting, 28 days earlier
indicators.note: Now: 1% cut, 24% rise; a month ago: 5% cut, 27% rise.

explain.what: Whether markets now expect the Fed to cut or raise interest rates at its next meeting, compared with a month ago.
explain.why: Interest rates set the price of every other asset; expectations move long before the Fed acts.
explain.score: Rate expectations have moved less than 15 points.

indicators.name: 10-year real interest rate, 20-day change
indicators.note: 2.93% on 30 Sep 2026 vs 2.44% on 1 Sep 2026. FRED publishes a day late.

explain.what: Whether the 10-year US interest rate after inflation (the inflation-protected Treasury yield) has risen or fallen over the last 20 trading days.
explain.why: Gold pays no interest, so when safe bonds pay more after inflation, holding gold costs more. 9 of gold's 10 worst weeks in 5 years were rate or dollar shocks.
explain.score: Real interest rates are rising: holding gold costs more.

explain.what: Whether the inflation that bond markets expect over the next 10 years has risen or fallen over the last 20 trading days.
explain.why: Gold is bought as protection against inflation; rising expectations tend to draw buyers.

indicators.name: Central bank gold buying, last 4 quarters
indicators.text: -20.5% (4 quarters to Jun 2026: 780 t vs 981 t)
indicators.measured: the 4 quarters before, both on WGC's latest published figure for each quarter
indicators.source: World Gold Council Gold Demand Trends (quarterly; typed in)

explain.what: How much gold the world's central banks bought in the last 12 months vs the 12 months before.
explain.why: Central banks have been gold's steadiest buyer since 2022 and buy regardless of interest rates; their pace sets a floor under the price.
explain.score: Central banks are buying less: weaker support if other buyers step back.

indicators.name: Consumer demand: jewellery plus bars and coins
indicators.measured: same quarter a year earlier, in tonnes
indicators.source: World Gold Council Gold Demand Trends (quarterly; typed in)

explain.what: Tonnes of gold bought as jewellery and as bars and coins (mostly China and India) vs the same quarter a year earlier.
explain.why: Shows whether everyday buyers still take metal at today's price; in tonnes, so high prices themselves push it down.
explain.score: Consumers are buying less metal: the price is rationing demand.

indicators.name: Western investor demand: GLD tonnes, 60-day change
indicators.note: 1,056.5 tonnes on 1 Oct 2026 vs 1,002.5 tonnes on 8 Jul 2026. GLD only, not all gold funds worldwide.

explain.what: Whether Western investors have added or removed gold through GLD over the last 3 months (60 trading days).
explain.why: A slower read of investor demand than the 20-day flow: sustained buying through a falling price is a sign of conviction.
explain.score: Investors have kept adding gold over 3 months.

indicators.name: GLD vs its 200-week average
indicators.note: $382.76 vs a 200-week average of $274.50.

explain.what: How far GLD is above or below its average weekly price of the last ~4 years (200 weeks). A stretch measure, not a valuation: gold has no earnings.
explain.why: Only extremes matter: in 2006–2026, weeks 60%+ above this average (top 5%) were followed by flat returns; moderate stretch was not a warning.
explain.score: Within its normal range of stretch.

indicators.name: Gold ÷ S&P 500 ratio
indicators.source: Yahoo Finance weekly prices (gold futures, S&P 500)
indicators.note: Ratio 0.548 (gold $4,202 ÷ S&P 500 7,666, week of 28 Sep 2026) vs a 10-year median of 0.476 (520 weeks).

explain.what: The gold price divided by the S&P 500 index, compared with its middle value over the last 10 years. A stretch measure, not a valuation.
explain.why: Shows whether gold is dear or cheap relative to stocks, the main alternative use of the money.
explain.score: Gold vs stocks is within its normal 10-year range.

lead: GLD's reading is building history (today's zone: Sell, −34 on a −100 to +100 scale): rising real interest rates and a firmer dollar are pressing on gold, while investors keep adding to GLD on the dip. Read it as a pressure gauge, not a timing signal.
bullets: Rates are the main pressure. The 10-year real interest rate is 2.93% on 30 Sep vs 2.44% on 1 Sep (+0.49 points, bearish); the dollar index rose 2.54 points over 20 trading days (bearish). The price trend is down. $382.76 is 8.0% below its 200-day average and the 50-day average is 4.8% below the 200-day (both bearish); over 3 months GLD is 1.6 points behind the S&P 500 (neutral). Price trend bucket −72 on −100 to +100.

Demand is mixed, and one figure tips it to Sell. Central bank buying is 20.5% lower over 4 quarters vs the 4 before (780 t vs 981 t, bearish), mostly because WGC moved 187 t of Q1 2026 into another category, so it counts at half weight (6 of 12 points) until WGC's Q3 report; on WGC's first Q1 figure it would be neutral and the composite about −27 (Hold). Consumer buying is 10.1% lower vs a year earlier (bearish); GLD's gold holdings rose 5.4% in 60 trading days (bullish). Demand bucket −41.
Not stretched to an extreme. GLD is 39.4% above its 200-week average (bearish only at 60%+) and gold vs the S&P 500 is 15.2% above its 10-year median (bearish at 25%+). Valuation (stretch) bucket 0.

Stretch (G-VL1): the 200-week average counts the current week twice (Yahoo repeats it): $274.48 instead of $273.42, so +38.7% instead of +39.3%. The score is unaffected (bearish only at 60%+); engine fix pending.
Fed odds (LQ6) use the shared engine's 28-day window and are jumpy: rise odds were 48% on 29 Sep and 34% on 30 Sep; on 29 Sep LQ6 would have read bearish (composite about -36).

5-year weekly replay (research/sanity_check.md): Sell readings in 2021-26 were followed by GLD +12.9% over 6 months on average vs +10.8% for all weeks; stretch at extremes was the best input, real rates the weakest.
